title: Refine UI V2 into a customizable Sakura Agent Messenger
goal: Refine the existing opt-in UI V2 into a chat-first, lightweight game-messenger experience with Sakura theme, soft bubbles, plain background, profile-sourced avatar, user customization, and measurable performance checks.
context: UI V2 shell was merged in PR #546 and profile-avatar rendering was merged in PR #547. Do not duplicate either implementation. The current V2 inbox and ChatScreen still expose heavier scaffold/panel treatment; refine existing screens in small verified slices.
forbidden_changes: Do not change Agent Runtime, policy, permissions, provider routing, workspace execution, or conversation persistence.
Do not remove the UI V2 opt-in toggle or change the V1 default before physical-device acceptance.
Do not duplicate the profile avatar store; profile.avatar.data remains the single source of truth.
Do not decode avatar bytes inside each message bubble or on every streaming update.
Do not add dependencies, background timers, continuous animations, remote wallpaper loading, or decorative particle effects.
Do not claim tests, CI, IPA build, or physical-device smoothness unless the exact result is observed.

implementation_plan.scope: Reduce visual weight in the V2 inbox and chat: remove redundant glass/panel nesting where practical, keep conversation content and composer dominant, retain access to workspace/tools through an explicit secondary action.
acceptance_criteria: Opening UI V2 lands on Messages and the primary visual focus is the conversation list or active conversation, not a dashboard or stacked cards.
The active chat keeps a compact header, scrollable message list, and persistent composer.
Search, new conversation, agent selection, export, rename, and other existing chat actions remain reachable.
The existing V1 UI remains available through the persisted UI V2 toggle.

implementation_plan.scope: Add a small semantic chat-theme layer with Sakura as the default V2 appearance, soft rounded message bubbles, and a plain static background.
acceptance_criteria: V2 defaults to a restrained Sakura palette with readable text and accessible contrast in light and dark appearance.
Message bubbles use soft rounded corners and distinguish user from Agent messages without gradients or heavy glass effects.
The default background is plain and static; no wallpaper image, particles, blur stacks, or always-running animation.
Theme selection is persisted and changing theme does not alter conversation or Agent state.

implementation_plan.task: PAUI-003C — Profile avatar and identity consistency
implementation_plan.scope: Use existing profile.avatar.data and cached avatar implementation across V2 inbox and chat; add invalidation only where missing.
acceptance_criteria: Profile avatar appears consistently in the chat/inbox locations where a user avatar is shown.
Changing or clearing the profile photo updates visible avatars without relaunching.
Missing or invalid image data falls back safely to the existing system avatar.
Avatar decoding is bounded/cached and does not occur per message row or streaming update.

implementation_plan.scope: Expose compact controls for theme and bubble style without bloating the main chat screen.
acceptance_criteria: Users can select supported themes and bubble styles from Profile or Settings.
Settings persist across app relaunch and changes preview immediately.
The chat screen itself remains free of customization panels unless explicitly opened.
Unknown or missing preference values fall back to Sakura / soft / plain.

implementation_plan.scope: Add or update targeted tests where the architecture supports them, run repository gates, then request physical-device checks.
acceptance_criteria: Swift package tests pass on the final PR head.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
No new dependencies or unbounded work in SwiftUI body/render paths.
Physical iPhone verification checks scrolling, sending while streaming, theme switching, avatar changes, and V1/V2 toggling.
Do not declare smoothness or release readiness until device checks are recorded.
The five implementation slices are completed independently and each slice passes its stated checks before the next is merged.
UI V2 remains opt-in until physical-device acceptance.
The shared KernelSession and all existing Agent execution/security behavior remain unchanged.
The final report links commits/PR and states exact CI and device verification status; no IPA is claimed unless an artifact exists.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA on the exact final PR head.
Record physical-device checks separately from CI.
recovery: Keep each UI change isolated. If scrolling, streaming, avatar refresh, or theme changes regress, revert only the latest slice while preserving the existing V2 toggle, shared session, and current chat execution behavior.
